_about.purpose: Seven multi-step OWASP Juice Shop challenges, classified by the LINKS each needs and this engine's coverage of each link. The value of this artifact is the per-link coverage column, which is checked against the engine's own tables by tests/test_chaining/test_needs_chaining_classification.py — so it cannot quietly drift as classes are added.
_about.premise_status: UNVERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE INSTANCE. The repository contains no pre-existing NEEDS_CHAINING list (grepped: no match anywhere in src/, tests/, docs/). This classification was derived from the chain-kind taxonomy in src/clinkz/chaining/ plus Juice Shop's published challenge set. Which challenges a given Juice Shop build actually ships, and whether each solves the way described here, is a question about a running target and is deferred to the Phase-5 live gate. Nothing in src/ reads this file; it is an analysis artifact and a test fixture, which is also why it lives in tests/fixtures rather than in src/ — a methodology must never carry a benchmark's vocabulary.

coverage_vocabulary.confirmed_today: This engine has a methodology that confirms this link's defining effect today, and it is dispatchable.
coverage_vocabulary.chain_carriage: This link is the composition itself, proven by the chaining decoy control (P4).
coverage_vocabulary.lead_only: A methodology exists and reaches this observation, but its defining effect is not witnessable by this engine, so it produces an unproven lead.
coverage_vocabulary.no_methodology: No methodology reaches this link at all.

challenges.label: Login Support Team
challenges.mechanism: A support-team credential is disclosed in an artifact the application serves; authenticating with it is the second step.

required_links.description: Recover credential material from a served artifact
The application accepts the recovered credential as authentication, while an equivalently-shaped decoy is refused

challenges.label: Forgotten Developer's Backup File
challenges.mechanism: A path-traversal primitive reaches a backup file outside the served directory; the credential material inside it is then used to authenticate.

required_links.description: Read a file the application does not intend to serve
The application accepts a credential parsed out of that file, while an equivalently-shaped decoy is refused

challenges.label: Forged Signed JWT
challenges.mechanism: Key material is recovered from a served artifact, a token is rebuilt under the application's own scheme, and the server accepts it while refusing a same-shaped control.

required_links.description: Forge a token under the application's own scheme and have it accepted while a broken-signature control is refused
The application serves the impersonated principal's own view to the forged token

challenges.label: Forged Coupon
challenges.mechanism: The coupon encoding is recovered from client-reachable code, a valid code is rebuilt, and the application accepts it at checkout.

required_links.description: Recover the plaintext scheme behind an opaque token the application issues
The application accepts a value rebuilt under that scheme while refusing a same-shaped random control
Apply the accepted coupon to a basket and complete the order

challenges.blocking_gap: The third link needs a completed checkout, which is a state-changing flow the client-safe rails refuse on a real target. It is reachable only under an explicit benchmark profile naming the payment and cancellation categories.

challenges.label: Reset a named user's password via their security answer
challenges.mechanism: The answer to a security question is recoverable from public application data; the forgot-password flow then accepts it and issues a new credential.

required_links.description: Recover the security answer from data the application itself publishes
The reset flow accepts the recovered answer and issues a credential

challenges.blocking_gap: Link 1 is OSINT over application content: reading a product description or a review and matching it to a person's security answer. That is a semantic association this engine has no methodology for, and inventing one that guessed would send password-reset requests against a real account.

challenges.label: Manipulate another user's basket
challenges.mechanism: An identifier belonging to another principal is accepted on a write, so an item is added to a basket that is not ours.

required_links.description: Cross an authorization boundary on a read to establish that another principal's object is addressable
The same identifier is accepted on a WRITE, and the object is read back carrying our value while a control that omitted it does not

challenges.blocking_gap: Both links are confirmable, but they compose through an identifier rather than through a carried secret, so the decoy-substitution oracle does not apply: an equivalently-shaped decoy identifier may legitimately name a real object. This chain is planned and reported as a lead rather than confirmed.

challenges.label: Server-side request forgery reaching an internal service
challenges.mechanism: A confirmed fetch primitive is pointed at an internal address, and content that address serves comes back.

required_links.description: Confirm the server fetches a URL we choose
Content from an internal address returns through the channel, while an equivalently-shaped non-resolving decoy address returns none of it
